_meta.evidence_classes: M measured, V vendor/manufacturer, S official statistic, F institutional forecast, B benchmark, A assumption

retained_blog._source: Merilehto (2026a), Gasum blog, 5 Oct 2026; BESS chart and text (https://www.gasum.com/fi/uutiset-ja-asiakastarinat/blogit/2026/suomen-sahkomarkkinan-jalkiteollinen-vallankumous--datakeskusten-tulo-vaatii-joustoa-muilta-markkinatoimijoilta/)

reserve_pool._source: Fingrid reserve market day 2026 (procurement cost 2025); Emaldo/Clean Horizon (revenue per MW)

usd_per_eur_2025.source: Bank of Finland, average annual exchange rates 2025

cost_anchor_2025._source: BNEF Energy Storage System Cost Survey 2025 via Energy-Storage.news (16 Dec 2025)

europe_yoy_decline_2025.note: Europe system cost fell 37% y/y in 2025; used only to back-cast 2024 for validation

bop_install_share.note: Installation/EPC/BoP uplift on turnkey equipment. Low = 0 covers the case that the BNEF turnkey figure already includes it. Anchored to Ember (2025): ~$75/kWh equipment + ~$50/kWh installation and connection for 4 h+.

grid_connection_eur_per_kw.note: Ember 2025: grid connection USD 30-100/kWh at 4 h; DEA: PCS + connection EUR 0.4-0.5 M/MW. Flat in real terms.

fixed_om_share.unit: fraction of equipment capex per year

tso_storage_fee_eur_per_kw_yr.source: Fingrid 2026 energy storage capacity fee 1,137 EUR/MW/a (>1 MW)

economic_life_yr.note: Vendor warranties up to 20 yr (Megapack 3), Fluence 25-yr service guarantee; Lazard 20 yr with augmentation; NREL ATB 15 yr (with augmentation in FOM). Low = short life (high cost).

connection_cost_drift_per_yr.note: Grid connection and civil works are assumed not to follow battery learning.

method_A_exogenous._source: BNEF (2025) Europe 4 h 2035 forecast for 2025-2035; NREL (2025) low/mid/high ratios thereafter
method_A_exogenous.note: Central 2035 = 101 / (Europe 4 h 2025); central 2050 = central 2035 x NREL mid 178/234. Low/high = NREL low/high relative to the 2024 baseline 334 $/kWh.
method_A_exogenous.note_2050: Central 2050 = BNEF 2035 index x NREL 2025 mid ratio 178/243 (NREL Table 2; its Section 3 text gives 234). Kept as a comparison path; the model uses method C.

method_B_experience._source: Ziegler & Trancik (2021); Our World in Data (2026); Schmidt et al. (2017)

doublings_2025_2035.note: Doublings of cumulative global Li-ion output from end-2025 (4.7 TWh; secondary compilation + Benchmark 2025 demand), IEA GEVO 2026 CPS/STEPS/NZE-type outlooks; derived

method_B_experience.note: Single-index Wright's law applied to cells only (comparison path).

method_C_component._source: This study, calibrated in model/research/component_calibration_reference.py. Reproduces BNEF Dec 2025 2035 4 h turnkey for Europe (USD 101) and China (USD 41).

cell_2025_eur_per_kwh.source: LFP storage cells EXW China late 2025 (Ember 2025; BNEF lowest LFP cell USD 36/kWh)

freight_duty_eur_per_kwh.source: Benchmark Q3 2026: EXW USD 53-58 vs CIF Europe USD 63-67/kWh; EU duty 0-2.7%

dc_bos_2025_eur_per_kwh.source: racks, BMS, thermal, enclosure; NREL 2025 cabinet split

bos_pcs_learning_rate.source: NREL 2025 implied ~8% (PCS), ~12% (cabinets); Schmidt et al. 16+-3% utility systems

cell_floor_eur_per_kwh.source: LFP cathode incl. Li 42-46% of cell cost (SMM); assumption

cell_cycle_premium_high_2030.note: lithium-cycle premium on cells in the high-cost case, peaking 2030, zero at 2025 and 2035

premium_decline_to_2035.source: central matches BNEF's implied Europe-China gap USD 104 -> ~60/kWh by 2035

near_term_index.source: China system prices +10-25% in 2026 (CNESA, EnergyTrend); export VAT rebate 13% -> 6% (Apr 2026) -> 0% (Jan 2027)

install_decay_per_yr.note: installation/EPC as an absolute cost (share of 2025 equipment), not scaled by learning

augmentation_share.source: industry practice 15-20% initial overbuild or augmentation in years 5-7; required with a 20-year economic life

cell_cost_multiplier_after_2030.note: 1.0 in all reported states; used by stress cases for a cheaper post-LFP chemistry (0.5) and a bound with free cells (0)

cycle_life.note: Full cycles to 70-80% SoH. PNNL 2022 warranty baseline 10,000 cycles at 80% DoD (~8,000 FEC); Megapack 3 >=10,000; CATL/HiTHIUM >10,000 claimed (V). Field fade 2-3%/yr (Figgener et al. 2024; Andreotti et al. 2026).

replacement_cost_eur_per_kwh_2025.note: DC block / pack replacement. BNEF 2025 stationary pack $70/kWh (=62 EUR); Europe packs ~56% above China.

charge_price_eur_per_mwh.note: Average price paid for charging energy; set by the market module later.

aux_kw_per_mwh.source: Enertis/ESN design figure 1.7 kW/MWh (central anchor); Dimovski et al. 2026 Italian air-cooled plant 3.3 kW/MWh (high); 4% of throughput at ~200 cycles/yr = 0.9 kW/MWh (low); liquid-cooled 5 MWh block 2.2-4.4 kW/MWh in winter (OEM). No Nordic field measurement.
aux_kw_per_mwh.note: Revised 17 Nov 2026 from 2.5 (1.5-4.5); declines with vintage (thermal design).

validation_projects._note: Disclosed Finnish contract values used as out-of-fit checks, not as calibration targets.

mertaniemi.boundary: EPC/turnkey supply incl. installation and commissioning; owner costs (grid connection) not included
mertaniemi.source: Merus Power release via Inderes, 16 May 2025

tervola_varevaara.boundary: Battery system + hybrid controller + maintenance/lifecycle services; 'over 8 MEUR'

forecast._note: Inputs for the five forecast methods. Triangular parameters are [low, mode, high]. Units GW unless stated.

start.note: Fingrid 424, 14 Nov 2026; GWh assumes 1.9 h fleet average (blog: ~3 GWh at 1.6 GW in Aug 2026)

observed_2026._source: Fingrid Q3/2026 text (Jan ~1.0 GW) and Fingrid open data 424 (monthly max, >1 MW units)

m1_pipeline._source: Blog (Merilehto 2026a): operating+FID 3.9 GW by end-2028; Renewables Finland (9 Sep 2026): 0.995 GW / 2.8 GWh under construction, ~1.7 GW permitted, 11.9 GW / 36 GWh planned in total

fid_remaining.note: 3.9 GW (blog, operating+FID end-2028) minus 2.092 GW operating
fid_remaining.cod_note: Schedule implied by blog text: (3.6-2.092)/1.808 = 0.83 in 2027, 0.17 in 2028; with ~25-30% of capacity slipping one year (A) this gives the 0.6/0.4 used here.

permitted_net.note: 1.7 GW permitted minus FID projects not yet under construction (0.813 GW) to avoid double counting

sources.eps_own: Savelli 2026 (Energy J.): +10% BESS -> -8% profit; Spain 2026 (Energy Reports): -54% spread at 30 GWh
sources.eps_flex: Savelli 2026: +10% RES -> +15% BESS profit (2030), fading by 2040; Dumitrescu et al. 2024
sources.pool: this study, reserves + balancing energy 2026 annualised (reserves.py, balancing.py)
sources.consumption: Fingrid Q3/2026 (2035: 110-162 TWh); Long-term Climate Plan (2050: 134-180 TWh); upper tail to 200 TWh for data-centre growth
sources.cap: Fingrid vision 2040 maximum (31 GW) ~ storage connection enquiries (>30 GW)

m3_equilibrium.pool_eligibility_note: FCR-N needs 1 h each direction with 34% reservation and FCR-D a 20% reservation (Nordic TSOs 2025); Fingrid LER/NON-LER split at 2 h (reserve market day 2026); a 1 h unit is limited to FFR/FCR-D and part of aFRR/mFRR.

committed.note: Blog: operating + FID 3.9 GW by end-2028 minus 2.092 GW operating (Nov 2026). Built regardless of the equilibrium (decisions taken).

m3_equilibrium.duration_tilt_note: Margin growth exponent for duration d is eps_flex x (1 + tilt x log2(d/2)): longer durations gain more from VRE/demand growth (multi-hour spreads). Anchors: Fingrid Q3/2026 4-8 MWh/MW; Danish Energy Agency AF25 2 h -> 6 h by 2050; Landy et al. 2026 4 h optimal (UK). Range includes 0 (no tilt). Class A.
m3_equilibrium.grid_forming_note: Co-located grid-forming BESS required for weak-grid wind/solar (Fingrid VJV2024: +-10-30% of plant capacity where ESCR<1). 0 / 0.8 / 3.0 GW by 2050 (A), ramped linearly from 2026; added to the stock at 1 h; compete with market batteries at weight 0.5.
m3_equilibrium.eps_pool_sat_note: Elasticity of the euro size of the reserve and balancing pool to the flexible fleet (batteries plus competing capacity), for given flexibility need. Evidence: hourly reserve-capacity cost fell 71% (2023-26) while battery capacity grew about fivefold; the combined pool fell 47% in 2026 as the fleet doubled (both also reflect demand growth). Class M/A.
m3_equilibrium.warranty_note: No retirement before 10 years (typical product warranty 10-20 yr); Weibull after, with mean life 15 -> 20 yr. Class V/A.
m3_equilibrium.cannibal_basis_note: 'power': arbitrage cannibalisation by fleet GW (central, matches the capacity elasticity of Savelli 2026); 'energy': by GWh, a stress case.

global_gw._source: IEA WEO 2025 STEPS ~900 GW 2030 (secondary); BNEF ~1,200 GW 2030; IEA CPS/STEPS/NZE 1.4/1.7/2.9 TW 2035; BNEF NEO 2026 2.0 TW 2035, 3.84 TW 2050; IRENA 1.5C 4.1 TW 2050; 2040 interpolated (A)

m4_topdown.share_note: Now: 2.09 GW / ~455 GW global end-2026 (end-2025 ~275 GW + 2026 additions ~180 GW, BNEF). Electricity share 0.30% (85 TWh / 28,200 TWh, IEA 2026).

peer_per_capita_2050_kw._source: Danish Energy Agency AF25: 6.8 GW 2050 / 5.99 M; Svenska kraftnat LMA2026: 8.3-9.4 GW 2050 / 10.6 M (secondary, unverified); populations [verify]

peer_now._note: approximate 2024-25 population and electricity consumption (national statistics; S, approximate)

m4_topdown.peer_note: Central: peers scaled by population. Scaling by present electricity consumption (Finland uses about twice as much per person as Denmark) is reported as a pool sensitivity rather than pooled, because it compares 2050 peer capacity with present consumption.

m5_envelope._source: Blog 2027-2028 (operating+FID .. +planning); Fingrid Q3/2026 2030 and 2035 (Moderate..High); Fingrid vision 2040 (7/11/31 GW; the 2 GW scenario is already exceeded and excluded)
m5_envelope.treatment: Discrete equal-weight mixture over the published states (low/mid/high, comonotone across years) with +-10% uniform jitter; 2030/2035 mid = midpoint of Fingrid Moderate..High.

operation_projection.cycles_note: Fingrid 398 discharge Jun-Oct 2026 = 13-19 equivalent cycles per month at 1.9 h (fleet_ops.py) -> 160-230 /yr

m2_diffusion._note: Logistic stock through two anchors: N(T0)=2.092 GW (Nov 2026, M) and N(end-2028)=M1 realised committed stock (sample-wise). Saturation K sampled; r follows from logit(N/K) linear in t.
m2_diffusion.k_source: lower bound Fingrid 2030 Moderate (4 GW, nearly committed); upper bound Fingrid 2040 vision high and M3 connection cap (31 GW)
m2_diffusion.pooled_note: With the implied r (10-90% time 6-15 yr), the logistic is near K by ~2038; later checkpoints carry the saturation prior (A).

duration_model._note: Fleet GWh for top-down methods (M2, M4): existing 3.97 GWh, committed 1.808 GW x 2.8 h, then net additions at new-build duration d_new(t), linear from 2.8 h (2027) to d_new_2050; stock declines scale GWh proportionally.
duration_model.d_source: low: M3 without duration tilt (2 h); central: M3 central 2050 (4 h), Landy et al. 2026; high: Fingrid Q3/2026 scenario 4-8 h, Danish Energy Agency AF25 6 h (F/A)

ensemble.weights: equal per available method (linear opinion pool)
ensemble._note: Constant method set from 2035 so that state paths do not jump when a method drops out. M1 only to 2030 (queue horizon). M4 from 2035 (top-down shares ignore the committed queue: its 2030 median 3.4 GW is below the 3.9 GW already committed). After ~2038 M2 sits at its saturation level K and M5 is extended flat at Fingrid's 2040 vision states (both class A: long-run levels).
ensemble.weights_note: From 2040 M2 (saturation prior bounded by Fingrid's 31 GW) and M5 (Fingrid's 2040 states) share one method's weight, because both rest on the same institutional anchor.
